* **Memory:** Uses groupshared memory for staging, reducing global memory bandwidth pressure [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that shell data (including centre, cutoff, l, AO count, and primitives) is staged in groupshared memory per chunk. It further explains that this staging allows the inner loop to execute using this memory, thereby 'avoiding dependent global loads per shell.' Avoiding dependent global loads directly reduces the pressure on global memory bandwidth, as the data is loaded once into faster shared memory and reused by multiple threads within the group.
